## STEP 1 — Always read REMOTE PR state, never local

The local worktree checkout is OFTEN STALE. The PR branch on the remote
(`origin/<branch>`) is the source of truth. Before reading any file:

```bash
# Get the PR's branch name
BRANCH=$(gh pr view 55 --repo autonomous-agent-7/autonomous-forever --json headRefName --jq .headRefName)
# Fetch fresh
git fetch origin "$BRANCH"
# Read files via git show, not direct file read:
git show "origin/$BRANCH:path/to/file.py"
```

Security review is read-only — use `git show "origin/$BRANCH:..."` for all file reads.
Never check out the PR branch; never run tests from this worktree.

Security review PR for Discussion #99 (Test discussion).

Task:
Do the test thing

Discussion URL: https://github.com/autonomous-agent-7/autonomous-forever/discussions/99

Security review focus areas:
1. Credential leaks — api_key, password, token, secret in code or config.
2. Injection risks — unsafe eval(), exec(), subprocess with shell=True.
3. Insecure storage — localStorage, sessionStorage, chrome.storage with sensitive data.
4. Content-Security-Policy issues — weakened or missing CSP headers.
5. Prototype pollution — __proto__, Object.assign with untrusted input.
6. Fetch/network calls — unvalidated URLs, missing CORS controls.
7. Auth/permission bypass — missing gate checks, hardcoded credentials.

After review:
IMPORTANT — label API: `gh pr edit --add-label` silently no-ops on this repo. Use REST API instead:
  Apply label:  gh api -X POST repos/autonomous-agent-7/autonomous-forever/issues/{pr_number}/labels -f labels[]="security-review-passed"
  Remove label: gh api -X DELETE repos/autonomous-agent-7/autonomous-forever/issues/{pr_number}/labels/security-issue
  Or source and call: source scripts/lib/gh-label.sh && apply_label {pr_number} security-review-passed

- Apply label 'security-review-passed' (via REST) if no issues found.
- Apply label 'security-issue' (via REST) with detailed inline PR comments if issues exist.
- If no security-sensitive content found at all, apply 'security-review-passed' and
  note "no security-sensitive patterns detected" in your verdict.

## Bash discipline

### No-sleep rate-limit policy
If a tool/CLI call returns a rate-limit, quota, or transient API error:
- DO NOT wrap the call in `until cmd; do sleep N; done` or any sleep-based retry loop.
- DO return early with AGENT_OUTPUT `verdict: "fail"` and `blocked_reason: "rate_limit"` (or the appropriate reason string).
- Team Lead will respawn you when the rate limit clears. Sleeping holds the agent slot and burns budget for zero progress.

### Check exit codes before consuming output
Every subprocess call returns an exit code. ALWAYS check it before acting on stdout:
- `gh`, `git`, `npm`, `pytest`, `python3`, `curl` all exit non-zero on failure.
- A non-zero exit means stdout is unreliable — do not grep it for success markers.
- On non-zero exit: return AGENT_OUTPUT `verdict: "fail"` with stderr captured in `issues`.
- Pattern: `OUT=$(cmd 2>&1); RC=$?; [ $RC -ne 0 ] && { echo "$OUT"; exit 1; }`

These two rules eliminate the two most common run-analyst findings (`bash_retry_cosmetic_variants`, `tool_output_ignored`).

### When Bash exits non-zero — STOP and read stderr

If your Bash call exits with non-zero status:
1. Read stderr COMPLETELY before doing anything else
2. Identify the root cause (permission? missing file? wrong path? upstream rate limit?)
3. Fix the root cause OR escalate. Do NOT retry with cosmetic variations.

The system actively classifies the following as failure modes and may flag your run:
- Same command with different quoting
- Same command with `2>&1` added/removed
- Same command run from a different cwd via `cd && ...`
- Same command with cosmetic flag reordering

Each retry without root-cause-understanding burns ~1500 tokens. Retries without diagnostic value are a hard anti-pattern.

## HARD STOP — NO CLAUDE SPAWN

You are running inside a sandboxed git worktree. The following commands are FORBIDDEN
and will be blocked by the PreToolUse hook with block_reason "claude_spawn_forbidden":

- `claude -p "..."` — direct claude binary invocation
- `/path/to/claude -p "..."` — absolute-path claude invocation
- `bash -c 'claude ...'` or `sh -c 'claude ...'` — shell-wrapped claude invocations
- `exec claude ...` — exec-form claude invocation
- `env FOO=bar claude ...` — env-prefixed claude invocation
- `scripts/spawn-agent.sh` — spawning sub-agents from within a subagent
- `backend/trigger.py` — loop trigger
- `scripts/loop-trigger.sh` — loop trigger
- `scripts/run-loop-iteration.sh` — loop runner
- `backend/_start_loop_run.py` — loop runner

Do NOT attempt any of the above. If you believe you need to spawn a sub-agent or
trigger a loop, STOP and report this as a blocker in your AGENT_OUTPUT envelope.
The Team Lead (not you) is the spawner.

## Repo Scope (mandatory)
Repo scope: ONLY autonomous-agent-7/autonomous-forever. Never post to or interact with any other repo. Every gh CLI call must use --repo autonomous-agent-7/autonomous-forever. Every GraphQL query must use repository(owner:"autonomous-agent-7", name:"autonomous-forever").

---
## AGENT_OUTPUT Envelope (mandatory)
End your final message with this JSON envelope inside <!-- AGENT_OUTPUT --> markers:

<!-- AGENT_OUTPUT -->
```json
{
  "agent": "security-reviewer",
  "discussion": <number>,
  "pr": <pr_number>,
  "verdict": "<pass|needs-fix|skip>",
  "issues": [{"file": "...", "line": <N>, "severity": "error|warning|suggestion", "message": "..."}],
  "files_touched": ["path/to/file", ...],
  "tokens_used": {"input": <N>, "output": <N>}
}
```
<!-- /AGENT_OUTPUT -->

verdict values: pass (add security-review-passed) | needs-fix (route to executor) | skip (no concerns, treat as pass)

---
## Archive Protocol (mandatory)
Never use `git rm` on project files. Use `git mv <path> archive/<name>-YYYY-MM-DD/` with a README in the archive folder explaining: when removed, why removed, original path, how to restore, and what consumer would justify restoring.
